title: Scope by an owned public network
explanation: Restrict indexed results to a network.
options: This is a reserved documentation range, so no useful results are expected. Replace it only with your approved public range.

title: Select one service port
explanation: Add a port constraint to the network scope.
options: Filters narrow the same query. A port number does not prove which application is running.

title: Quote a multiword organization
explanation: Use quotation marks around a filter value containing spaces.
options: Organization metadata may identify a hosting provider rather than the asset owner.

title: Filter country metadata
explanation: Filter the indexed geolocation country.
options: Country uses a two-letter code. IP geolocation is not a precise physical address.

title: Search a banner term
explanation: Search the default banner text within scope.
options: An unqualified word does not search every structured field.

title: Use a structured product filter
explanation: Filter Shodan's identified product metadata.
options: Detection may be incomplete or mistaken; compare raw evidence.

title: Find indexed hostnames
explanation: Find records associated with a hostname pattern.
options: example.com is a documentation placeholder. Hostname matches are leads, not conclusive ownership evidence.

title: Exclude a service port
explanation: Remove port 80 records from a scoped query.
options: A leading minus negates this filter. Confirm behavior with the current filter reference.

title: Search HTTP title metadata
explanation: Find a title string within the approved scope.
options: Titles are reusable and can be deceptive; they are not proof of ownership.

title: Inspect certificate subject matches
explanation: Filter certificate subject common-name metadata.
options: A certificate subject alone is not proof the endpoint belongs to that organization; modern names also occur in SAN fields.

title: Create an isolated Shodan environment
explanation: Create a dedicated Python environment for the CLI and SDK.
options: Create kali-lab first. If venv support is missing, install python3-venv with apt.

title: Activate the environment
explanation: Select the environment in this shell.
options: Repeat in each new terminal; deactivate leaves it. This is not a Windows command.

title: Install the official Python client
explanation: Install the SDK and bundled CLI inside the active environment.
options: Requires internet. An isolated environment avoids changing Kali's system Python.

title: List CLI subcommands
explanation: Inspect the installed client's command list.
options: Use command-specific help for options that vary by release.

title: Read API-key setup help
explanation: Inspect how CLI authentication is configured.
options: Initialization requires your own API key and saves it locally. Do not put a real key in this book, shared output or literal shell history.

title: Check account information
explanation: Ask Shodan about the authenticated account.
options: Requires prior CLI initialization. Available features and credits depend on the account.

title: Count a scoped query
explanation: Request the indexed result count without downloading banners.
options: A result count is not necessarily a unique-device count. Documentation-range queries normally return no useful data.

title: Preview a few indexed records
explanation: Retrieve a small bounded result set.
options: This queries Shodan, not the target hosts. Filtered searches can consume query credits.
result: Selected fields from up to five results.

title: Download a bounded export
explanation: Save up to 100 indexed records for offline work.
options: Filename comes before the query. The CLI writes compressed JSON; inspect its reported filename. May use query credits.
result: A JSON.gz export if results are available.

title: Read parse options
explanation: Inspect local-file parsing features.
options: Parsing an existing export does not repeat the remote search.

title: Read the synthetic export
explanation: Extract fields from the fictional sample created in Guided Lab 20.
options: No API key is needed for this local parsing exercise.

title: Count unique addresses in an export
explanation: Count distinct nonempty address output from the sample.
options: The supplied sample contains two IPs but three services. For other exports, validate missing fields before counting.

title: Extract observation times
explanation: Inspect when each synthetic banner was observed.
options: Observation time is not necessarily the date you downloaded the file.

title: Export simple delimited fields
explanation: Write the sample's simple fields to a local file.
options: There is no header. General text fields can contain commas or newlines; use Python's csv module for robust CSV serialization.

title: Request a count using the SDK
command:
import getpass
import shodan
api = shodan.Shodan(getpass.getpass("Shodan API key: "))
result = api.count('net:198.51.100.0/24')
print(result['total'])
explanation: Authenticate without embedding the key in source text.
options: Run in the environment containing shodan. The hidden prompt keeps the key out of code and shell history, but the process holds it in memory.
result: An indexed result count or API error.

title: Summarize ports with facets
explanation: Request a small aggregation instead of full records.
options: The api object comes from the preceding SDK example. Facet counts describe matching records, not verified assets.

title: Bound a paginated result stream
command:
from itertools import islice
query = 'net:198.51.100.0/24'
for banner in islice(api.search_cursor(query), 100):
    print(banner.get('ip_str'), banner.get('port'))
explanation: Consume at most 100 records from the SDK's paginated iterator.
options: Iteration makes API requests and can consume credits. A cap on records does not mean one request per record.

title: Inspect monitor management help
explanation: Read the installed client's monitoring command group.
options: Creating monitors is a separate account action with plan-dependent capacity. Help does not create an alert.

title: Inspect on-demand scan help
explanation: Read available scan-submission options without submitting a scan.
options: Unlike a database lookup, on-demand scanning asks Shodan to contact targets and uses separate scan credits.

title: Inspect host-lookup help
explanation: Read host lookup and historical-data options supported by this build.
options: A lookup retrieves indexed observations; history access may depend on the plan. Use an owned public address for any actual lookup.
